channel.title: Up First from NPR
channel.description:
NPR's Up First is the news you need to start your day. The three biggest stories of the day, with reporting and analysis from NPR News — in 10 minutes. Available weekdays at 6:30 a.m. ET, with hosts Leila Fadel, Steve Inskeep, Michel Martin and A Martinez. Also available on Saturdays at 9 a.m. ET, with Ayesha Rascoe and Scott Simon. On Sundays, hear a longer exploration behind the headlines with Ayesha Rascoe on "The Sunday Story," available by 8 a.m. ET. Subscribe and listen, then support your local NPR station at donate.npr.org.

Support public media by joining NPR+ at plus.npr.org. You’ll get perks for over 25 NPR podcasts, including sponsor-free listening for Up First, NPR News Now, and more.

item.title: AI Stocks Tumble, Permitting Reform Bill Clears Senate, Confusion Over Medicaid Cuts
item.description:
Financial markets suffer major losses as concerns over an AI bubble grow. A bipartisan bill that would speed up energy construction projects and weaken environmental regulations clears the US Senate. Confusion grows over new Medicaid work requirement rules set to begin in January.

item.title: Government Funding Pressure On Iran War, National Security & Tech, Iowa Detonation
item.description:
Democrats are weighing whether to use the government funding deadline to cut off money for the war in Iran, exposing divisions over how quickly the party should act.
The Trump administration approved sales of advanced U.S. chips to Chinese companies, including some the Pentagon has linked to China’s military, fueling a debate over whether those sales help America compete or create new security risks.
The Army delayed plans to destroy thousands of pounds of unstable bomb-making material in Iowa after public pressure and a lawsuit, even as officials warn colder weather could make it more dangerous.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: Ben Shapiro reassesses the president he campaigned for | Newsmakers
item.description:
Conservative host Ben Shapiro says he is holding to his conservative values in the unstable era of President Trump.

The host of The Ben Shapiro Show voted against Trump in 2016 but also campaigned for him in 2024. He’s disappointed in the president’s tariffs, alleged corruption and the execution of the Iran war.

“I regret the way the president has performed,” Shapiro tells host Steve Inskeep in this episode of Newsmakers. “I don't regret my vote. I don't have a time machine.”

Shapiro says Trump’s aggressive immigration enforcement and the general “whiff of corruption” that surrounds the White House — specifically the Trump family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial — all contributed to the Republican Party’s midterm losses in Congress, governor's mansions and state legislatures.

He believes that Republicans have an “uphill road in 2028” and that Vice President Vance isn’t the ideal Republican presidential candidate. He argues that Vance would shrink Trump’s winning 2024 voting bloc of Hispanics, the working class, women and college-educated individuals.

Shapiro points to Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a potential 2028 Republican candidate with broader appeal and a larger coalition. But he says many within the current White House will likely be damaged by association.

Shapiro also unpacks his new movie, Confession — featuring Rob Lowe and James Franco — and the recent decline in his show’s YouTube subscriptions.

item.title: Trump Trilateral Summit In China, House Democratic Leadership, Anthropic IPO
item.description:
President Trump met with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together for the first time, but the meeting produced no major breakthrough as tensions remain over Ukraine, technology and Taiwan.
House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to become the next Speaker and are already laying the groundwork for investigations into President Trump’s inner circle as they prepare to take control of the chamber.
Anthropic begins trading publicly after the biggest IPO in history, testing how much appetite investors still have for artificial intelligence amid growing concerns about an AI bubble.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: Trump-Xi-Putin Meeting, Nvidia Board Rejects Haung's Return, Computer System Outages
item.description:
President Trump meets Xi Jinping in China as the two countries remain locked in disputes over trade, rare earths and advanced technology, before Vladimir Putin joins them for a three-way summit aimed partly at projecting global leadership.
Nvidia's board says Jensen Huang will not return as CEO, even as the company posts another huge quarter and its interim leadership tries to reassure investors that the chipmaker can stay on top without its founder.
Apple, the National Security Agency, the FAA and major banks have all suffered recent computer outages, raising questions about why so many critical systems are breaking down at once.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: FAA Tech Upgrade Update, Trump Asia Agenda, Petition To Reinstate Huang At Nvidia
item.description:
Another technology problem disrupted United Airlines flights on Monday night as President Trump pushes Congress for more money to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system and Democrats question how previously approved funds are being spent.
Trump is in Asia for a historic summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, after the White House said Ukraine would be off the agenda and Trump later said he plans to discuss it.
Silicon Valley leaders are rallying around ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as pressure grows on the company’s board to reconsider his resignation while questions about the scandal and Nvidia’s future remain unresolved.

item.title: FAA Ground Stop Update, Democratic Leadership Contest, Trump's Travels To Asia
item.description:
Airlines are recovering from a nationwide ground stop caused by a failure during routine FAA maintenance, raising new questions about the aging air traffic control system just ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer to lead Senate Democrats, arguing the party’s midterm wins should not mean a return to business as usual.
President Trump heads to Asia for meetings with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, where the White House says he plans to focus on nuclear weapons while leaving Ukraine and tensions over artificial intelligence off the agenda.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: What universal free childcare is costing New Mexico
item.description:
A year ago, New Mexico became the first state to offer universal free childcare. Parents who have successfully enrolled their children in the program say it's changed their lives. But many families have yet to see the other side of a waitlist. On this episode of The Sunday Story, NPR’s Julie Depenbrock reports on how the demand for childcare is outpacing providers’ capacities and the state budget. Can New Mexico catch up and bring the program to the finish line?

item.title: Air Travel Ground Stop, Starship Rocket Launch, ExxonMobil Eyes Return to Venezuela
item.description:
Federal officials say telecommunication outages were to blame for the nationwide ground stop that paralyzed air travel on Friday, but offered few details about what caused the issues. SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. American oil giant ExxonMobil eyes a return to Venezuela as President Trump continues to promise historic oil deals in the South American nation.
